verdicts.tldr: Escaping <gno-button after the bracket walker breaks a pointy link, whose bare brackets then bind to the realm's own reference and footnote definitions; the output is no longer idempotent
verdicts.details: escapeBracketsOutsideLinks spares `[evil](<gno-button x>)` as a link, then escapeGnoButtonTags inserts a backslash that turns the pointy destination into a non-pointy one containing a space, so goldmark drops the link and `[evil]` resolves against the realm's `[evil]: https://realm.example/home` (or `[^evil]` against its footnote). The raw input binds to nothing, and at base the same input stays escaped-safe and idempotent, so the diff introduces it. The rollout half holds too: under head gnoweb the mainnet (= base) native lets 28 of 35 gno-button goldens render live anchors. Fix: run escapeGnoButtonTags over the whole input before escapeBracketsOutsideLinks and drop the two in-loop calls; ship the native before, or gate, the gnoweb button extension.

verdicts.tldr: gnoweb turns <gno-button> on unconditionally while the escape protecting sanitized content lives in a native mainnet only gets at a chain upgrade
verdicts.details: ExtButtons.Extend(m) runs in GnoExtension.Extend with no option, and the mainnet native is byte-identical to the merge base's, which passes <gno-button verbatim. A head gnoweb deployed against mainnet before the upgrade therefore renders sanitize.Block output such as 'hi <gno-button href="/r/evil$help&func=Drain" label="Claim" variant="caution" />' as a realm-styled transaction button, which the PR's safety claim says cannot happen. Fix: gate ExtButtons behind a gnoweb option left off until the upgrade carrying the native, or state and enforce the ship order.
